educationalAssessment.sourceParity: B4 matches supplied PDF and official AO. Vascularity is a risk mechanism rather than automatic osteonecrosis. SNAC wording allows preserved radius-proximal-fragment/radiolunate articulations and avoids uniform full-radioscaphoid progression. PDF's no-arthritis variant clue is explicitly qualified by a primary case with arthritis; no silent absolute adopted. Existing A2/B2 PDF/AO wording difference remains visible and qualified.
educationalAssessment.translationParity: DE/EN/FA preserve B2/B3/B4, distal-to-proximal direction, risk versus proof, may versus certainty, no recalled trauma versus exclusion, missing bony bridging, arthritis distribution and individual feedback. No clinically material language omission or negation/number reversal found. FA runtime rendering remains untested.

primarySourcesFreshlyRead.read: Actual Herbert classification section: A1/A2, B1–B5, C and D. B2 complete waist, B3 proximal pole, B4 fracture-dislocation. No automatic treatment instruction added from the classification label.

primarySourcesFreshlyRead.type: Official AO Surgery Reference proximal-pole definition
primarySourcesFreshlyRead.read: Actual definition/imaging/pitfall/vascularity paragraphs. Main dorsal distal vascular entry, retrograde proximal supply and ischemia/osteonecrosis/delayed-union/nonunion vulnerability. Supports risk mechanism, not certain necrosis from B3 alone.

primarySourcesFreshlyRead.type: Vender et al.1987 original64patient radiographic cohort
primarySourcesFreshlyRead.read: Complete original abstract: symptomatic untreated nonunions; radial/midcarpal degeneration and radius-proximal scaphoid/radiolunate preservation. Historical article uses SLAC terminology for nonunion-associated pattern; packet labels it SNAC in the supplied-PDF/current teaching context. Cohort percentages/timepoints not generalized or taught as individual certainty. Fullarticle not read.

primarySourcesFreshlyRead.type: Doman/Marcus1990 original longitudinal congenital bipartite case
primarySourcesFreshlyRead.read: Complete original abstract: bilateral congenital bipartition followed from early ossification to skeletal maturity; MRI helpful for distinguishing traumatic nonunion. Packet does not infer that one MRI/sign always establishes the diagnosis.

primarySourcesFreshlyRead.type: Richards/Ledbetter/Transfeldt1987 original bilateral bipartite case with osteoarthritis
primarySourcesFreshlyRead.read: Complete indexed original abstract (direct open supplied only HHS footer): no trauma history, symmetric bipartition and distal-ossicle/radial-styloid degeneration with preserved proximal articulation. Directly supports that arthritis is not an absolute exclusion of congenital bipartition. Fullarticle not read.
